title: VectorLane — Hosted Embeddings + Rerank API Walkthrough
summary: Intro demo of Redwood hosted embeddings + reranker for VectorLane search. Walkthrough included API calls, sample rerank pipeline, Console tuning workflow, and Optimize recommendations (batching, cache, model variants). Discussed integration with existing vector store, SSO/KMS requirements, and pricing/next steps for pilot and security docs.

transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood Inference, AE on the account. we got Owen from solutions here too. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Priya Nair: Hi, Priya here — head of search at VectorLane.
[00:11] Ethan Cole: Ethan, CTO.
[00:12] Jamal Ortiz: Jamal, data eng.
[00:13] Sofia Ruiz: Sofia, PM.
[00:16] Owen Reyes: Hey all, Owen — I'll run the demo. Quick agenda, we'll do a short intro, show hosted embeddings + rerank flow with console tuning tips, then Q&A and next steps.
[00:28] Maya Chen: Goals from our side: show an end-to-end hosted pipeline, highlight latency/cost levers in Optimize, and answer security questions you flagged.
[00:35] Priya Nair: Sounds good. main thing for us — we have a global product, strict p95 latency targets for search, and cost matters — we serve a lot of queries. We also use Pinecone today for vectors, and want to know how Redwood fits without ripping out infra.
[00:49] Owen Reyes: Great. quick architecture — hosted API handles embeddings generation, then candidate fetch from your vector DB (like Pinecone/Weaviate), then Redwood reranker endpoint takes top-K candidates plus query and returns ranked results. We support both dot/FAISS-derived vectors and you can keep your vector store as-is.
[01:10] Jamal Ortiz: So our flow today: client -> frontend -> our API -> Pinecone -> we rerank clientside using a small transformer. We're trying to move ranking closer to the server to reduce client complexity and improve feature-rich reranking. latency target p95 ~ 220ms end-to-end for rerank path.
[01:27] Owen Reyes: Okay that helps. Demo will use a small dataset so numbers won't be production, but we'll point to how batching, prefix/KV cache, and smaller model variants reduce token cost and improve tail latency.
[01:38] [02:00] Owen Reyes: (screen share) starting in Console — here's the API Playground. We have an embeddings endpoint and a rerank endpoint. I'll show a sample call. first, embeddings: POST /v1/embeddings with model redwood-embed-compact, payload query text. simple JSON, returns vector.
[02:22] [02:30] Owen Reyes: Now candidate fetch mock: we send vector to Pinecone and get top 50 ids, then call Redwood reranker with the query and the 50 doc snippets. here's the rerank call — note fields: query, candidates[], schema for document metadata, and optional model hints (we'll select redwood-rank-2-small).
[02:48] Priya Nair: Do you stream rerank results? what about partial scores?
[02:52] Owen Reyes: Rerank returns a scored list; we don't stream tokens like generation. it's a single response with ranks and scores. our Console shows token-level breakdown for embeddings generation cost and rerank inference cost separately so you can attribute money to each stage.
[03:10] Ethan Cole: For 220ms p95, what's realistic? our client is in us-east.
[03:14] Owen Reyes: With hosted, typical rerank p95 for redwood-rank-2-small with top-50 is around 80-150ms depending on snippet length; embeddings call ~15-35ms. But that's model-dependent and influenced by batching. Our Optimize tab will recommend batch size and KV cache (prefix caching) based on your query distribution.
[03:34] Sofia Ruiz: What's prefix/KV cache?
[03:36] Owen Reyes: It's the KV cache for autoregressive models — for rerank models it's more like cached embeddings for repeated queries or cached doc embeddings on our side if you choose to pin them. For LLM generation, KV cache avoids recomputing earlier tokens. For rerank we support document embedding caching so you only generate embeddings for changed docs.
[03:58] Jamal Ortiz: We already store document embeddings in Pinecone. if we keep that, is there double-cost?
[04:02] Owen Reyes: No, if you keep embeddings in Pinecone, you can skip Redwood embeddings step and only call reranker. Alternatively, you can use Redwood embeddings to replace your vector store pipeline and store in your DB — options are flexible.
[04:14] [04:30] Owen Reyes: Demo call — I'll run a real rerank with a mock top-10. (runs) Here's a sample response: list of doc ids and rerank scores, with brief explanation on why the model bumped doc X (Console highlights attention).
[04:50] Priya Nair: Console shows "explain"? that's helpful for triaging.
[04:53] Owen Reyes: We have a simple explain feature that surfaces tokens or phrases the model attended to most — it's heuristic and sometimes noisy.
[04:59] Ethan Cole: Security — what about data retention and encryption? we need SOC 2 plus KMS integration, and logs for audits.
[05:06] Maya Chen: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II. We provide KMS integration for private deployments and hosted with BYOK for enterprise customers; audit logs and request-level tracing are in Console. I'll attach the SOC2 summary and our security whitepaper.
[05:22] Priya Nair: Are request payloads stored? we have to avoid storing customer queries in plaintext for 90 days.
[05:27] Maya Chen: By default we retain logs for short windows for debugging, but enterprise pilots can opt out of retention, or set redaction. We also offer Private (VPC) deployments if retention policy can't be relaxed.
[05:40] Jamal Ortiz: On infrastructure — how does fallback work if a model variant is down? we need graceful degradation.
[05:45] Owen Reyes: Smart routing: requests can failover from a high-perf replica to a smaller cheaper variant. Redwood supports canarying and automatic fallback to compatible quantized models so your app sees a result even if perf model is overloaded.
[05:59] Priya Nair: And billing — is it per token for reranker?
[06:03] Maya Chen: Rerank is priced per API call plus per-token compute for the embedding/generation portion. We'll provide an example pricing sheet. For pilots we often cap spend and provide trial credits.
[06:15] [06:30] Owen Reyes: Back to Console: Optimize tab here suggests batch size 8 for our traffic pattern, and cache TTL of 12 hours for doc embeddings. It estimates 27% cost savings and 18% p95 improvement for the sample workload.
[06:45] Priya Nair: How do you measure quality/regression? we can't afford rank regressions when changing models.
[06:51] Owen Reyes: We have evals tied to prompt sets — you can upload a labelled validation set (query + ideal doc ranking) and Console will run A/B tests and monitor NDCG/precision changes across model rollouts. It will block a rollout if quality drops beyond threshold.
[07:09] Ethan Cole: Integrations — we run k8s on GCP with private networking. can Redwood call into our Pinecone instance over VPC peering?
[07:16] Maya Chen: For hosted API we support private networking options through Redwood Dedicated or Private (VPC) with secure connectors. For pilot we often use mutual TLS and IP allowlists; for production we recommend VPC connectors.
[07:30] Jamal Ortiz: Latency with a VPC connector — any overhead?
[07:33] Owen Reyes: Minimal. There's an extra hop but usually within a 5-15ms window depending on region. We'll quantify during pilot.
[07:42] [08:00] Priya Nair: Show us an example where we keep Pinecone and call Redwood only for reranking — how do we pass metadata?
[08:06] Owen Reyes: In the rerank payload you can pass an array of candidate objects: {id, text, metadata}. We'll accept up to 100 candidates inline; larger sets can be referenced by id and Redwood will fetch if you give us a read-only connector.
[08:22] Sofia Ruiz: Connector — is that a service account we hand you?
[08:25] Maya Chen: It's read-only credentials with limited scope. We can also accept pre-signed fetch URLs for docs.
[08:32] [09:00] Owen Reyes: (runs a small script) here's a notebook run: 1) embed query (if desired), 2) fetch top 50 from Pinecone, 3) call rerank endpoint with top 50 docs. I'll paste the exact curl/snippet to the chat.
[09:20] Jamal Ortiz: If we have long documents, do you chunk?
[09:23] Owen Reyes: Yes, we recommend chunking at ingestion and storing chunk embeddings. Reranker can accept score-collapsed results to map chunk scores back to parent doc. Console has a chunking template and recommended chunk size per domain.
[09:38] Priya Nair: We have a multi-lingual dataset — will rerank work for non-english?
[09:43] Owen Reyes: We support multiple languages in our embeddings models. Reranker models are trained primarily on english but we have multilingual variants; quality varies. We'll run a quick evaluation if you share a sample set.
[09:56] [10:30] Ethan Cole: Benchmarks — can you run our 1k sample queries against your hosted instance? we want real p95 numbers.
[10:35] Maya Chen: Absolutely — that's a standard pilot step. Owen will help run the benchmarks; we'll need your sample set and an account or temporary API key.
[10:45] Owen Reyes: For the pilot we usually do a 30-day sandbox with capped spend. We'll use your sample queries, pin a model variant, and gather p50/p95/p99 plus cost estimates.
[10:56] Priya Nair: How do we handle personalization signals? we enrich candidate docs with feature metadata — can reranker consume those features?
[11:02] Owen Reyes: Yes, candidate objects can include metadata fields, numeric features, recency, user-level signals. Reranker can accept structured features and we can pass them into the scoring architecture. Note: features affect tokenization overhead slightly if embedded as text.
[11:20] Jamal Ortiz: Any limit on candidate size?
[11:23] Owen Reyes: There's a practical size: up to ~100 candidates inline with reasonable snippet lengths. We recommend returning short snippets and the rest of doc in metadata.
[11:34] [12:00] Priya Nair: What's the friction for rolling to production? we want to start with a small endpoint, then scale.
[12:06] Maya Chen: You can start with hosted pilot (no infra changes), then move to Dedicated once you need reserved capacity and tighter SLAs, or Private for VPC/on-prem. Rolling is a config change — you pin model versions and set rollout policies in Console.
[12:18] Sofia Ruiz: Do you support canarying by percent of traffic?
[12:21] Owen Reyes: Yes, Console supports per-route canarying and automatic rollback if metrics degrade.
[12:27] [13:00] Owen Reyes: Quick note about cost optimization: choose smaller rerank models for lower-latency use cases, use cached doc embeddings to skip recompute, and batch rerank requests when feasible. Optimize will simulate cost savings and show token-level breakouts.
[13:20] Priya Nair: For mobile clients, can we batch multiple queries from a session?
[13:24] Owen Reyes: You can create batched rerank requests server-side; client should send session-level hints. Batching improves throughput but may add latency for small QPS.
[13:36] [14:00] Ethan Cole: Any customers who've migrated from using only Pinecone + client-side rerank to your hosted rerank?
[14:05] Maya Chen: Yes — a retailer moved rerank server-side and saw 30% lower client complexity and 20% improvement in ranking quality due to richer model features. I'll get you a reference.
[14:15] Priya Nair: Ok that helps.
[14:18] [14:30] Owen Reyes: Now I'll show the Console Relevance Lab: you can upload eval sets, run A/B, and get NDCG plots. here's a run where model B slightly improved NDCG@10. you can set alert thresholds.
[14:48] Jamal Ortiz: Will you run continuous evaluation?
[14:50] Owen Reyes: Yes, Console can run scheduled evaluation jobs or ad-hoc. You can wire alerts to Slack.
[14:57] Sofia Ruiz: Are alerts per-route?
[15:00] Owen Reyes: Per-route and per-model.
[15:04] [15:30] Priya Nair: One more on security — SSO, RBAC? we have internal access controls.
[15:34] Maya Chen: We support SSO/SAML, SCIM for provisioning, role-based access controls in Console, and audit trails.
[15:42] Ethan Cole: For compliance we'll need encryption-at-rest and in transit.
[15:45] Maya Chen: AES-256 for rest, TLS1.2+ in transit, and KMS for key management. We'll include the cryptography section in the package.
[15:57] [16:00] Owen Reyes: Quick Q&A lightning:
[16:03] Jamal Ortiz: Are retries idempotent?
[16:05] Owen Reyes: Yes, requests include idempotency keys for most write operations.
[16:08] Priya Nair: Can we run a smoke test in our staging?
[16:10] Maya Chen: Yes — we'll provide staging credentials for pilot.
[16:12] [16:30] Owen Reyes: I'll paste the notebook, the curl examples, and a link to Console Relevance Lab into the chat now. (pastes)
[16:42] Priya Nair: Seeing the examples is helpful. question — do you support rerank explanations as structured tokens or just text blobs?
[16:50] Owen Reyes: Mostly text heuristics today; structured saliency is on the roadmap. Some customers export token-level saliency via the SDK.
[16:58] Sofia Ruiz: Timeline — if we approve the security docs this week, can pilot start next week?
[17:02] Maya Chen: Yes, timeline is tight but doable — pilot kick-off next Tuesday possible.
[17:12] Ethan Cole: Any risks for us?
[17:14] Maya Chen: Main risk is model quality mismatch; we'll mitigate via evals and pinned rollouts. Also network setup for connectors might take a few days.
[17:26] [17:30] Owen Reyes: Recap: demo'd embeddings + rerank flow, Console Optimize recommendations, evals and monitoring, and security options. We'll run benchmark with your 1k sample once you share it.
[17:42] Priya Nair: Next steps noted. we'll get the sample set and security questionnaire back.
[17:48] Maya Chen: Great — I'll share the SOC2, security whitepaper, pilot pricing, and Owen's rerank notebook. Thanks everyone.
[17:55] Ethan Cole: Thanks.
[18:00] Jamal Ortiz: Thanks all.
[18:04] Sofia Ruiz: Bye.
[18:10] (call ends)
